newsitem.title: USA: North Dakota prepares for spring flood.
newsitem.headline: North Dakota prepares for spring flood.

text.p: Residents of North Dakota's snowbound Red River Valley prepared on the first day of spring Thursday for what experts believe could be the worst flooding in a century.

Hardware stores did a brisk business in pumps and drain plugs to hold back the expected sewage backup and foam footballs ideal for stuffing up toilets were in short supply. Many residents in this city of 75,000 have dug deep troughs between towering snowdrifts, hoping to guide the runoff away from their houses.

"The problem is, then it becomes someone else's problem," said Donald Schwert, a geologist at North Dakota State University who is helping officials disseminate flood information. "The snow is not hard to move, it's just that there's so much of it and there's nowhere to put it."

The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration issued a warning this week that spring flooding could be more widespread this year than in any year in the past decade -- especially in the upper Midwest.
More than 20 people have died in flooding this month in the Ohio River Valley. Rain running off frozen ground has inundated homes across several states.

Experts agree there will be flooding this spring along the slow-moving Red River, which flows north across a glacial plain into Canada's Lake Winnipeg. The depth of the flood will depend on how quickly the record snow melts and whether additional precipitation compounds the problem.

"We will have a flood this year," Schwert said. "Very little of the snow has melted yet." Up to nine feet of accumulated snow on the eastern third of North Dakota contains the equivalent of three to seven inches of rainwater, he said.
"We have at least one flood per year, but most of these have been relatively minor," Schwert said. "This one is anticipated to be the greatest flood of the 20th century."
